title: Control Plane operational sprint bootcamp - notes
content:
Meeting: Control Plane operational sprint bootcamp - half-day sync
Date: 2026-11-02
Facilitator: Asha Patel
Attendees: Asha, Daniel, Riley, Sofia, Ben, Lina, Marcus (joined late)
Location: Zoom / #platform-controlplane slack / whiteboard

Objective:
- Rapid alignment on short-lived experiments for routing fallback, auth token caching, and quota soft-fail behavior before Friday canary.
- Surface any regressions from last week's rollout and assign owners for rollback/test plans.

Overview / context (30m)
- Quick recap of last week's routing weight changes: observed ~5% increase in tail latency for multi-tenant low-qps routes between 09:00-11:00 PT (PLT-1987). Not user-visible but impacts SLO p99 for internal metrics.
- Recent auth token caching change (PR: controlplane#412) introduced a race when tokens refresh concurrently; reproduced locally with heavy auth churn thanks to Riley's harness.
- Quota soft-fail: experiments to let low-priority routes receive best-effort tokens are currently in alpha; need to tighten telemetry to avoid overconsumption.

Notes / raw observations (freeform)
- Daniel: routing allocator appears to prefer newer nodes for multi-tenant routing which increases KV cache misses. Hypothesis: host affinity heuristic changed when we rolled allocator config. Need to confirm with allocation logs.
- Riley: auth race observed only when token TTL < 3s and > 1k auth requests/s per instance. Added unit test but integration fails intermittently.
- Sofia: quota soft-fail flagged multiple customers but billing shield prevented charge; need to ensure we surface quota hits to console and alerting without noisy pager noise.
- Ben: local canary harness shows fallback path is correct but metrics tagging inconsistent (route_id vs route_name). Hard to aggregate.
- Lina: SRE noticed increased OOM churn on a subset of dedicated nodes (looks related to a recent kernel upgrade). Will escalate to infra.

Decisions (quick)
- Pause any allocator config rollouts until we validate KV cache miss metrics (owner: Daniel, due EOD 2026-11-03).
- Revert the auth token change from PR 412 on canary for now; hotfix branch to be prepared and smoke-tested (owner: Riley, due 2026-11-03 morning).
- Keep quota soft-fail flagged in alpha but flip telemetry to DEBUG for now and enable sampled traces for 1% of requests to capture path (owner: Sofia, due 2026-11-05).

Action items (concrete)
- PLT-1987: Investigate tail latency bump and identify correlation with allocator heuristic changes. Daniel + Ben. Target: initial root cause hypothesis by 2026-11-03.
- PLT-2003: Auth token race reproduction and revert plan; create hotfix branch and run canary. Riley. Target: revert + canary by 2026-11-03 11:00 PT.
- Instrumentation: add route_name tag to fallback metrics and backfill last 24h (Ben). Add backlog ticket for metrics schema review.
- Quota telemetry amp: Sofia to add sampled traces (1%) and surface a dashboard widget for customer-impacting quota events. Target dash ready by 2026-11-04.
- Infra follow-up: Lina to open incident with infra team for OOM/upgrade correlation; map affected nodes and schedule safe node drain if needed.

Experiment plan (2-week window)
- Canary 1 (2026-11-04): auth revert deployed to canary pool; run ramp schedule 1% -> 5% -> 15% over 90m if p95/p99 stable. Rollback criteria defined in PLT-2003.
- Canary 2 (2026-11-06): allocator heuristic toggle behind feature flag; run only on dedicated pool with KV cache instrumentation enabled.
- Quota alpha: keep throttling rules but change soft-fail to sampled logging for 24h.

Risks / open questions
- If allocator revert is delayed, could impact SLAs for customers relying on steady p99 (esp tiered customers). Need contingency to pivot routing to alternate region.
- Auth revert may hide root cause if the race is exercised only in combined load scenarios; ensure preserved repro artifacts.
- Billing/console: exposing quota hits may create churn in CS—coordinate with Customer Success before enabling warnings (owner: Sofia to sync with CS).

Parking lot / follow-ups (not blockers for canary)
- Consider a small change to host affinity scoring to favor nodes with warm KV caches — longer-term; add RFC. (owner: Daniel)
- Postmortem of the kernel upgrade OOM correlations; include mitigations for future quick rollbacks. (owner: Lina + SRE)
- Short doc for engineers on how to read fallback traces and interpret tags. (owner: Ben)

Meeting artifacts & references
- Repro harness: github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/tree/tests/auth-harness (Riley)
- Allocator logs sample: s3://redwood-ops/controlplane/allocator/2026-11-01 (Daniel)
- PLT tickets: PLT-1987, PLT-2003

Notes-to-self (Asha)
- Prepare a 5-slide status snapshot for Monday AM sync: 1) what we reverted, 2) telemetry gaps, 3) canary schedule, 4) owner list, 5) blockers.
- Ping CS about potential customer-facing noise if quota telemetry surfaces warnings.

Next check-ins
- Short async update in #platform-controlplane by EOD 2026-11-03 (owners update ticket status).
- 30m follow-up sync 2026-11-03 09:30 PT to confirm auth revert canary and allocator investigation status.

Raw TODO (scratch)
- [ ] add metric tag mapping cheat-sheet
- [ ] schedule infra incident bridge if OOMs increase after kernel patch
- [ ] add fallback unit tests to CI with route_name assertions

End of notes.

-- end --
